column3: The Hebrew explicitly makes Eleazar the subject of bringing it outside the camp.
The Hebrew describes someone burning the heifer, using active verbs.
The Hebrew names scarlet without explicitly specifying wool and says to throw it into the midst of the burning.
The final expression identifies it as a sin offering, rather than explicitly saying “purification from sin”.
The Hebrew specifies a human dead body.
The Hebrew says his uncleanness is still in him.
The Hebrew includes everything in the tent, not only everyone.
The Hebrew says a dead person without explicitly specifying natural causes.
The water is literally called living water; the Hebrew does not include a separate command to put the ashes in the jar.
The final touching has no explicitly stated object in the Hebrew.
